title: Cluster Flow
intro: Where does gas collect as it flows through a galaxy cluster? Start with the glowing filaments, freeze the flow, and turn the cube to inspect a dense knot. You can also jump straight to the expanding-universe model, record a run for replay, or save an image or movie.
dataset: CAst for Windows with OpenGL 3.3 support. The simulation builds its own gas volume. You can start without any telescope images.
outcome: Explore gas in three dimensions, change the conditions that drive its motion, and save a view or a recording you can revisit.

groups.title: Open the lab and look around

steps.title: Open Cluster Flow
steps.requires: Start Citizen Astronomy (CAst). If another workspace is open, choose **Mode → Choose Mode…** to reach the mode picker.
actions: Scroll down to **Simulations**. Click the **Cluster Flow** card outlined in the screenshot.
steps.check: The workspace opens with **CLUSTER FLOW** above the controls. After the filament network is ready, a glowing gas distribution appears and the simulation time begins to advance.
steps.alt: The Simulations row of the CAst launcher with the Cluster Flow card outlined and numbered.

steps.title: Freeze the gas to examine a knot
steps.requires: [Open Cluster Flow](#launch). If you are in cache replay, [return to live](#return).
actions: At the top left, click **Pause**. Use one bright knot where several filaments meet as your landmark.
Read **Time** below the button. When you want gas to move again, click the same button, now labeled **Resume**.
steps.check: Pausing holds the simulated gas and its time at the current state. You can orbit or change the displayed field while it is paused. **Restart** rebuilds the initial gas distribution using the current Scene settings.
steps.alt: Live cluster density view with the Pause button marked beside the running gas volume.

steps.title: Turn the volume and look inside
steps.requires: A live or recorded volume is visible. [Pause the gas](#pause) if you want to follow the same knot as the camera moves.
actions: Place the pointer in the marked area of the picture. Hold the left mouse button, drag sideways, then release to orbit the cube.
Keep the pointer over the picture and roll the wheel to move closer or farther away. Hold the right mouse button and drag to shift a knot toward the center.
To get back to the opening view, expand **View** if needed, scroll the left panel, and click **Reset camera**.
steps.check: Foreground and background filaments shift relative to one another as you orbit. Zooming changes how close you are to the existing structures.
steps.alt: An outlined drag area on the live cluster image to the right of the camera controls.

steps.title: Rotate the camera automatically
steps.requires: Open **View → Camera motion** in the left panel. Camera controls also work on a [replayed recording](#scrub).
actions: Drag **Horizontal speed (deg/s)** a little to the right of the center for a positive speed. The center is zero.
Tick **Rotate horizontally** and watch the view turn around its focus. A negative speed turns it the other way.
Click **Stop camera motion** when a filament is at the angle you want to keep.
steps.check: The camera can circle the cluster even while the gas is paused. Stopping the motion keeps the current angle.
steps.alt: Camera motion controls with Horizontal speed, Rotate horizontally, and Stop camera motion numbered in order.

steps.title: Switch from density to temperature
steps.requires: Open **View** in a live or replayed run. Click the **Camera motion** heading to collapse it if you need more room.
actions: Click the arrow beside **Display field** and select **Temperature**. Compare the pattern with **Gas density**, which shows where gas collects.
If the field is too dim to inspect, move **Exposure** to the right a little. In the same menu, try **Gas speed** to see how fast gas moves or **Compression / shocks** to see where flows converge.
steps.check: The selected field name changes in the dropdown and the picture redraws immediately. The temperature image shown here highlights a different pattern within the same gas volume. Exposure changes the image brightness.
steps.alt: Display field set to Temperature and the Exposure slider marked beside the resulting gas image.

steps.title: Cut a thin slab through the cube
steps.requires: Open **View** and scroll the left panel until you see **Slice thickness**. Select **Gas density** under [Display field](#field) to match the example.
actions: Drag **Slice thickness** left from its full-width setting to about 0.40. The **Slice position** slider appears underneath.
Drag **Slice position** slowly in either direction to move the slab through the cube. To restore the whole volume, drag **Slice thickness** fully right.
steps.check: Some filaments disappear when they fall outside the slab. As you move the slab, different knots enter the picture.
steps.alt: Gas density rendered as a slab with Slice thickness and Slice position highlighted.

steps.title: Save the view as a PNG
steps.requires: Frame the picture you want in a live or replayed run. Expand **View**, then scroll the controls below **Ray samples**.
actions: Click **Save image...**. In the file dialog, choose a folder, enter a filename such as **cluster-density.png**, and click **Save**.
Open the PNG from the folder you chose to inspect the exported view.
steps.check: The PNG contains the rendered gas at the viewport’s dimensions. The chosen camera angle, display field, and slice are visible in the image.
steps.alt: Save image button marked at the bottom of the View controls beside the density image.

steps.title: Change the speed of evolution and cooling
steps.requires: Use the live **Cluster flow** model. Click **Resume** if the gas is paused. Collapse **View** and expand **Physics**.
actions: Drag **Evolution pace** left to ask the solver to advance less simulated time per second. Watch the **Time** readout above the panel.
For a cooling experiment, note the current **Cooling rate**, then drag its slider a little to the right. Use the [Temperature field](#field) to watch how the gas changes as time advances.
steps.check: The slider readouts change immediately. Cooling affects the evolving cluster gas, so give the simulation time to show the difference. Drag a slider back to its earlier value to restore that setting.
steps.alt: Physics section open with Evolution pace and Cooling rate highlighted beside the cluster.

steps.title: Trigger one outburst
steps.requires: Choose the live **Cluster flow** model and let the run advance. Expand **Physics → Outbursts**. The [Temperature field](#field) makes local heating easier to follow.
actions: Clear **Automatic outbursts** to control when the next event happens.
Check that **Outflow strength** is above zero. Leave the other outburst settings at their defaults for this trial.
Click **Trigger outburst** once and watch the gas around the two central halos over the next few simulation steps. Tick **Automatic outbursts** again to restore repeated events.
steps.check: The model injects heat and motion near the centers. How clearly a change shows up depends on the display field, time elapsed, and outburst strength.
steps.alt: Outbursts controls with Automatic outbursts, Outflow strength, and Trigger outburst marked.

steps.title: Choose how finely the solver steps
steps.requires: In a live run, expand **Physics → Timestep & solver**. Collapse **Outbursts** or scroll the panel to reach it.
actions: Open **Preset** and choose **Fine timesteps** to ask for smaller advances in simulated time. Read **Last step** below the controls while the run is advancing.
For manual control, drag **Maximum timestep** left. The preset changes to **Custom**. You can select **Balanced** from the preset menu to switch back to a preset.
steps.check: The preset and timestep readouts reflect the new settings. Shorter steps can take more computing time to cover the same span of simulated time.
steps.alt: Timestep and solver controls with Preset and Maximum timestep highlighted.

steps.title: Set the size and detail of a cluster
steps.requires: Use a live run. Collapse **View** and **Physics**, then expand **Scene**. If a recording is open, [return to live](#return) first.
actions: Set **Model** to **Cluster flow**. This model draws gas along filaments into fixed dark halos.
Drag **Cluster cube size (code units)** a little to the right. Read the estimated number of clumps and cell size immediately below the slider.
Open **Gas grid** to choose the number of cells along each side. A larger grid resolves finer structures and uses more memory. Keep the existing grid for a first run, then [apply the scene](#apply).
steps.check: The scene values update in the panel. As long as the change is pending, the gas in the viewport still belongs to the current run.
steps.alt: Scene settings with Cluster flow, Cluster cube size, and Gas grid numbered next to the current live volume.

steps.title: Try a cube of the expanding universe
steps.requires: In live mode, collapse **View** and **Physics** and open **Scene**. You can [return to live](#return) from any recording.
actions: Open **Model** and choose **Cosmological volume**. This model follows gas and dark matter as density variations grow in an expanding universe.

Inspect **Comoving cube size (Mpc)**. Keep the displayed size for a first run, or move the slider to choose the width of the simulated region. Leave the remaining cosmology settings at their defaults.
Scroll down within **Scene** and [apply the scene](#apply).
steps.check: Cosmology settings appear, including the cell size and starting redshift. The cluster can remain in the picture until you apply and restart.
steps.alt: Cosmological volume selected and Comoving cube size marked while the prior cluster is still displayed.

steps.title: Apply your settings and start the new scene
steps.requires: You have changed the [cluster settings](#cluster) or selected [Cosmological volume](#cosmology). Applying starts that live model from its beginning.
actions: Scroll to the bottom of **Scene** and click **Apply scene & restart** (marker 1).
Watch the amber **Scene changes pending** message (marker 2) disappear. Give the new grid time to appear. If **Resume** is showing at the top, click it to advance the new run.
steps.check: The pending message disappears. The live display uses the new scene. A cluster shows **Time** and **Box side** at the top. The expanding-universe model shows **Elapsed** and **z**.
steps.alt: Apply scene and restart button and its amber pending-change message at the bottom of Scene.

steps.title: Read time and redshift in cosmology mode
steps.requires: [Select Cosmological volume](#cosmology) and [apply the scene](#apply), then scroll the control panel to the top.
actions: Find the marked two-line readout under the playback controls. **Elapsed** gives time since the starting redshift in billions of years (Gyr). **z** gives the redshift.

If **Resume** appears, click it and watch the numbers as the run advances. **a** is the scale factor, a measure of how far the model universe has expanded. **Box** gives the width in comoving megaparsecs.
steps.check: As elapsed time increases, the scale factor increases and redshift falls. The example starts at z = 9 with a scale factor of 0.100.
steps.alt: The time, redshift, comoving box width, and scale factor marked above a freshly initialized cosmological volume.

steps.title: Set up a short practice recording
steps.requires: In a live run, scroll to **Bake** and click its heading to expand it. A bake computes a run from its starting conditions and stores selected states as frames.
actions: Drag **Evolution duration** left for a short trial. The cluster example uses about 0.35 in simulation units. In the cosmological model the label shows Gyr.
Drag **Cached frames** near the left end to save roughly 20 states. Set **Cached volume grid** and **Cached tracers** lower for a smaller file. You can use nearby values.
Read **Estimated cache** before choosing a file. More frames give you more moments to replay. A larger cached grid preserves more detail in each frame.
steps.check: The estimate updates as you change the settings. The example stores 20 frames at 32 cubed with 8,000 tracers for about 0.01 GB.
steps.alt: Evolution duration, Cached frames, and the estimated cache size numbered in the live Bake section.

steps.title: Bake the run to a .cflow file
steps.requires: Open **Bake** and [choose recording settings](#cache-settings). A bake uses the current Scene and Physics settings, including any pending scene changes.
actions: Click **Bake from start...**. Choose a folder, enter a new filename such as **filaments.cflow**, and click **Save**.
Wait for the cached-frame count to finish. If you need to stop early, click **Cancel bake (keep frames)** to retain the frames already computed.
steps.check: After a completed bake, the cache opens for replay. Its filename and frame count appear in **Bake**, along with a **Cached frame** slider.
steps.alt: The Bake from start button marked below the estimate for a 20-frame practice run.

steps.title: Open a recording you already have
steps.requires: You have a **.cflow** file from an earlier [bake](#cache-write). Open Cluster Flow and expand **Bake** in the left panel.
actions: Click **Open cache...**. Navigate to the folder containing your recording, select the **.cflow** file, and click **Open**.
steps.check: The selected filename and number of cached frames appear. Use the replay controls to visit a frame or play the recording.
steps.alt: The Open cache button marked in the Bake section of the live workspace.

steps.title: Find a frame or play the recording
steps.requires: A recording is open under **Bake**. [Open an existing file](#cache-open) or [bake a run](#cache-write) to get here.
actions: If the recording is playing, click **Pause replay** above the panel. Drag **Cached frame** (marker 1) to inspect a single saved state.
Click **Play replay** (marker 2) to advance through the frames. Use **Playback frames / second** in the Bake section to set the preview speed.
Tick **Loop replay** (marker 3) to play repeatedly. To return to the first frame and pause, click **To start** beside the playback button.
steps.check: The timeline moves through saved frames. You can still orbit the image and switch display fields while inspecting the same recording.
steps.alt: Recording named filaments.cflow with Cached frame, Play replay, and Loop replay numbered.

steps.title: Turn a recording into an MP4
steps.requires: [Bake a run](#cache-write) or [open a .cflow file](#cache-open), then expand **Bake** and scroll to the bottom of its replay controls.
actions: Choose **Movie resolution**, such as **1280 x 720**.
Set **Movie FPS**. Each cached frame becomes one video frame. For example, 20 frames at 10 FPS make a two-second video.
Click **Export MP4...**. Choose a filename with the **.mp4** extension and click **Save**. Wait for the export progress bar to finish before opening the file.
steps.check: The chosen folder contains a movie of the recording in your current view. Enabled camera rotation follows movie time during export. **Stop export (keep video)** finishes a shorter movie if you stop partway through.
steps.alt: Movie resolution, Movie FPS, and Export MP4 marked in the recording’s Bake section.

steps.title: Leave replay and edit the simulation
steps.requires: A cache is open and any movie export has finished. Expand **Bake** and scroll below **Loop replay**.
actions: Click **Return to live**. If you want the gas to advance, scroll to the top and click **Resume** if that button is showing.
Expand **Scene** to edit a new starting model, or **Physics** to change how the current live gas evolves.
steps.check: The cached timeline and movie controls disappear, and the live physics and scene controls are available again. Your saved .cflow file can be reopened later.
steps.alt: Return to live button outlined between the replay and movie controls.
